evidence: Plin. Ep. 7.21.4: gallīnam ut ā tē missam libenter accēpī
terms.comment: Of letters, gifts, news and payments; of news, accēpimus, “we are told” (Cic. Sen. 60).

phrases.latin: accēpī tuās litterās …; quās lēgī libentissimē plēnissimās amōris
phrases.english: I received your letter …, and read it with the greatest pleasure, so full of affection as it was

phrases.latin: gallīnam ut ā tē missam libenter accēpī
phrases.english: I was glad to receive the hen, as it came from you

phrases.latin: Beneficium dandō accēpit, quī dignō dedit.
phrases.english: whoever has given to someone deserving has received a kindness in the giving

sources: Cicero’s letters to Atticus checked against the Perseus Latin texts (9 November 2026).
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-plinius, loci-publilius, loci-cicero-philosophica), checked against the editions named there.
